changes: p3: affiliation and residence restated. 'hiraṇyabale sugatabāsasthānena' is read as 'living in the Sugata's abode (a vihāra) at Hiraṇyabala'. The vihāra goes in affiliation and Hiraṇyabala in residence.
Date: month normalised to 'Māgha'. Added a note on the chronogram and how it fits Guṇakāmadeva's reign. ce_approx 1185 confirmed: Māgha NS 305 falls in early 1185.
Notes: 'kalyāṇena' flagged as probably an auspicious adverb, not a personal name. Possible identification of Hiraṇyabala with Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra flagged as uncertain.

relations.evidence: śrīguna(!)kāmadevarāje |kalyāṇena hiraṇyabale sugatabāsasthānena samantabhadhrena svaya(!) lekṣi?

notes: The year is written 'triśate varaśavānayute': 300 plus a corrupt word-numeral, probably śara or bāṇa (= 5). That gives NS 305, as the cataloguer reads it. NS 305 falls within Guṇakāmadeva's reign (c. NS 300–316 / 1184–1196 CE), so the date fits. Māgha NS 305 is about January–February 1185 CE. 'kalyāṇena' just before the place phrase is probably an auspicious adverb ('auspiciously'), not part of a name. 'hiraṇyabale' could be a corrupt form of Hiraṇyavarṇa (Mahāvihāra, Patan), but this is unverified, so the place is left unnormalised. 'sugatabāsasthānena' describes the scribe as living in a vihāra. 'svaya(!) lekṣi?' = svayaṃ lekhi ('written by himself'). Ownership is not stated, so no owner role is added. Kalyāṇaśrīmitra is named as the compiler of the text (uddhṛta), so his role is author.
